summary: Internal NLB inserting PROXY protocol header breaks TLS handshake to serving instances in private deployment
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent TLS handshake failures from model-serving pods after migrating fronting NLB to 'preserve client IP' with PROXY protocol enabled. Impact: model artifact pulls and live streaming sessions fail with TLS errors causing request 5xxs and retries. Scope: affects a fraction (~10-15%) of serving pods behind the internal NLB; appears after the customer's recent network change to enable proxy-protocol on the NLB.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer enabled PROXY protocol v1 on internal NLB and preserved client IP option in NLB config
2) Deploy a model-serving pod behind the NLB that expects TLS from the client (no PROXY handling)
3) Initiate a model artifact fetch or start a streaming generation request via the private endpoint
4) Observe TLS handshake failures and 5xxs on a subset of requests; some connections succeed depending on pod placement and LB path.
logs: serving-pod stderr: 'tls: first record does not look like a TLS handshake'
NLB flow logs: 'target:10.10.12.58:443, client:203.0.113.45:52344, action: forward, proxy_protocol: enabled'
agent network capture (pod): 'TCP payload begins with 'PROXY TCP4 203.0.113.45 10.10.12.58 52344 443\r\n' followed by TLS ClientHello'
SDK error on client: 'rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed before full handshake'
comments: 2026-03-10 09:22 - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Customer opened ticket after enabling 'preserve client IP' on internal NLB during an internal migration. They report 5-10% of model pulls fail with TLS handshake errors. Asked for recent load-balancer config and pod logs.

2026-03-10 11:05 - Customer (SafeSend network admin): Confirmed NLB was toggled to enable PROXY protocol v1; sent NLB config snippet and flow logs. Provided pod logs showing 'first record does not look like TLS handshake'.

2026-03-10 13:40 - Eng (Marco Chen): Reproduced locally by injecting PROXY v1 header in front of our serving binary; observed identical 'first record does not look like a TLS handshake' from Go tls library. Hypothesis: serving process isn't expecting PROXY headers and fails TLS parsing.

2026-03-11 08:12 - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Suggested two immediate workarounds: A) disable PROXY protocol on the NLB, or B) enable PROXY protocol handling on the serving side via the sidecar/nginx that can consume proxy headers and pass TLS through to the application. Asked customer to test disabling PROXY protocol for a subset of targets.

2026-03-11 10:00 - Customer: Disabled PROXY protocol on the NLB for one target group. Error rate dropped to baseline within 15 minutes. Customer rolled back the NLB change across all target groups and reported service recovered.
investigation_notes: Confirmed root cause: internal NLB configured to insert PROXY protocol headers. Our serving processes accept raw TLS on port 443 and do not inspect/strip PROXY headers, so the PROXY header bytes are interpreted as the start of the TLS record, causing the Go TLS stack to reject the handshake.
Repro steps validated: injecting PROXY v1 line before ClientHello triggers the same error locally.
We observed partial impact because the customer's deployment uses mixed target groups and some targets had the NLB change applied while others did not; this explains intermittent failure rate.
resolution_summary: Immediate resolution: Customer disabled PROXY protocol on internal NLB and service recovered. Long-term options: 1) If customer needs to preserve client IP, configure the serving ingress to accept PROXY protocol (add a PROXY-aware TLS terminator such as HAProxy/nginx with 'proxy_protocol' enabled or update our edge sidecar to parse PROXY v1), or 2) use a TCP-level load balancer mode that preserves client IP without inserting PROXY headers where possible. Follow-up task created to document PROXY protocol behavior for Private deployments.
